qualifying_findings.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions | AI Act Service Desk
qualifying_findings.publisher: European Commission AI Act Service Desk

visible_dates.evidence: FAQ states that some AI Office and member-state enforcement powers start to apply on 2 August 2026; transparency obligations and GPAI rules are enforceable from that date.
FAQ states that from 2 August 2026 onwards, AI agents intended to interact with natural persons or generate content are subject to transparency rules.

qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The European Commission FAQ says AI Act enforcement powers begin on 2026-08-02 for prohibited practices, transparency requirements for certain AI systems, and general-purpose AI model rules. It also states AI agents are not a separate legal category but are covered by AI system and GPAI model definitions; agent interaction and generated-content transparency rules apply from 2026-08-02, and GPAI systemic-risk obligations include autonomous capabilities and agentic use considerations.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: EU AI Act enforcement for prohibited practices, Article 50 transparency obligations, GPAI model obligations, and agentic systems using GPAI models; pre-2026-08-02 generative AI systems have until 2026-12-02 for Article 50(2) marking and detection obligations.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This creates an active compliance and audit-evidence boundary for AI systems and agents: providers and deployers need user-facing transparency, generated-content marking paths, systemic-risk assessment, mitigation evidence, and enforcement-response readiness for GPAI and agentic deployments.

follow_up_actions: During ingest, map the official FAQ to local governance-and-compliance and agent-and-tool-security leaves without duplicating broad AI Act background.
Check whether a more specific official Article 50 Code of Practice or AI Office enforcement page should be linked as point-of-use source evidence.

visible_dates.evidence: Section 22757.6 is amended to state that the chapter becomes operative on August 2, 2026.
Large online platform and GenAI hosting platform provisions become operative on January 1, 2027.
Capture device manufacturer latent-disclosure provisions become operative on January 1, 2028.

qualifying_findings.factual_summary: California AB 853 amends the California AI Transparency Act so Chapter 25 becomes operative on 2026-08-02. The chapter covers provenance data and digital signatures for GenAI content, defines covered providers as publicly accessible GenAI systems with over 1,000,000 monthly California users, requires AI detection/provenance mechanisms under the underlying chapter, and adds later obligations for large online platforms, GenAI hosting platforms, and capture device manufacturers.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: California Business and Professions Code Chapter 25, AI Transparency Act; covered GenAI providers from 2026-08-02, with related platform and device provisions staged for 2027 and 2028.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The operative date turns synthetic-content provenance, disclosure, and verification into a live compliance and evidence concern for large GenAI providers operating in California, affecting authenticity controls, privacy handling for provenance data, third-party license revocation, and abuse-resistant detection tooling.
